To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
haploid wheat plants can regenerate from callus culture via somatic embryogenisis and that the regenerated plants were all haploid.
haploid plants of wheat can be regenerated from callus cultures and that this regeneration is possible in the long term.

(i) haploid callus cultures can be induced from young inflorescences of wheat, (ii) some of these callus cultures retain the capacity to regenerate plants via somatic embryogensis and/or direct differentiation of ovary-like structures for more than a year and (iii) all regenerated plants are haploid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method for haploid plant regeneration from callus cultures.
the development of a reliable method for the production of doubled haploid plants in the wheat variety "Svea".
the long-term maintenance of calli and plant regeneration in haploid wheat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
haploid wheat can be regenerated from calli derived from young inflorescence of pollen plants.
the callus cultures from the young inflorescences of haploid wheat plants were embryogenic.
the callus cultures of the wheat haploid plants can be maintained in a long term culture for at least one and a half year.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
haploid plant regeneration from callus cultures is a reliable method of haploid wheat production.
haploid plant regeneration from wheat callus cultures is possible.
haploid plants of wheat are able to produce calli from which somatic embryos are formed and plants regenerated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to regenerate plants from long-term callus culture of haploid wheat.
haploid plants can be obtained from callus cultures initiated from young inflorescences of haploid pollen plants.
haploid callus cultures are very stable in their capacity to regenerate plants.
